source_read: PDF pp. 717-723 (all pages; abstract and Tables 1-2 read on rendered pages 717 and 719, since the text layer turns digits into letters)

key_findings.note: p. 718: a mean of 26.9% (SE 1.0) of the 30 mg load was left in the device; 21.8 mg (SE 0.33) salt, 17.5 mg (SE 0.26) base; f = 0.903 (SE 0.104) in Table 1.
Geometric means are Table 1 footnotes b and c; the 8.3-18.2 h range is in the Results on p. 718.
Table 1 verified on the rendered page 719.
Table 2 verified on the rendered page 719.
p. 722: 125 (SE 14) and 105 (SE 20) ng/mL/h, no significant difference after correction for dose (P>0.7), 14-17% of the methamphetamine AUC, urinary amphetamine 18-20%, both on a molar basis.
p. 720: 38 (SE 9.8) for the smoked condition, cited to reference 4, and 41.5 (SE 20.1) intravenous; peaks at 18 (SE 2.1) and 17.4 (SE 1.1) min; heart rate at 11.8 (SE 1.6) and 12.6 (SE 2.8) min.

key_findings.correction: Rate constants are right (36.9, SE 7.5, and 0.693, SE 0.102 per hour) and the model fitted 4 of 6 profiles, but the absorption half-lives of about 1.1 and 60 minutes are printed by the paper itself (p. 722, immediately after the rate constants), so they are not an editors' calculation.

key_findings.note: p. 722: mean saliva-to-plasma ratio 6.0 after the intravenous dose with average coefficients of variation of 50.8%, and 5.1 from 4 to 24 h after smoking.

reporting_issues.note: Abstract 11.5 (SE 0.5) and 11.3 (SE 1.74) h against Table 1's 16.7 and 17.4 h. Recomputed from Table 1: 17,104/1,013 = 16.9 h and 13,546/787 = 17.2 h, so the table is the internally consistent pair.
Table 1 main column holds arithmetic means (11.8, 13.1 h); the geometric means (11.1, 12.2 h) used in the abstract are in footnotes.
The denominator (the amount removed from the device) appears first in the Discussion on p. 720.
The abstract states that the 67.2% (SE 3.1) oral figure is calculated from this study together with an earlier one.
Standard errors throughout Tables 1 and 2 at n = 6; the factor is the square root of 6, about 2.4.
The smoked subjective and cardiovascular values on p. 720 carry the reference marker for the earlier report on the same volunteers.

risk_of_bias.note: High is right and equals the worst domains. Same instrument caveat as Schepers for the senior author: no order, allocation or washout is described, so this is not a randomized or counterbalanced design in the sense of METHODS 5.3, and RoB 2 is being applied only because the design enum maps human-laboratory to it. Either document the exception on the card or re-appraise with ROBINS-I.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: Randomization process (order of the two conditions)
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Confirmed by reading the Methods (pp. 717-718): neither order, interval nor washout between the smoked and intravenous sessions is stated anywhere.
Open administration, no placebo, and the absorbed smoked dose (17.5 mg base) exceeded the intravenous dose (12.42 mg base) in Table 1.
All 6 contribute to both conditions; the two-input model fitted to 4 of 6 is stated by the authors and belongs under domain 5, where the card also records it.
Objective assays with the device residue recovered and quantified, against a self-anchored high rating in an open session.
No protocol; the two-input model was fitted after the plateau was seen; effects data partly deferred to the earlier paper.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is right. The acute-tolerance wording is the one claim that outruns the design, and the card names it; the tabulated pharmacokinetics match the text apart from the mean residence times.

missed: Denominator ambiguity extends beyond bioavailability: Table 2's percent of dose in urine (36.8% smoked, 45.0% intravenous) is computed against the administered base dose, that is against the 17.5 mg taken up from the device, while the abstract calls it the nominal dose (editors' calculation: 6.46/17.5 = 36.9%, 5.57/12.42 = 44.8%). Anyone reading 37% against the 30 mg placed in the device would be out by about a third.

Context the card does not carry for the 90.3% figure: in vitro, with a syringe in place of a person, 57.0% (SE 5.3) of a 40 mg load was recovered as trapped vapour and 44.8% (SE 2.7) remained in the device (p. 718), so the fraction of material placed in a device that can reach anyone is far below the bioavailability of what is taken up.
